headline: Approved earlier minutes with edits and supported hosting an e-bikes maintenance workshop; discussed snow removal and street sweeping.
summary: Director Ray Jodoin of the Department of Public Services discussed snow removal, contractor shortages, and street sweeping with the group. Members also discussed safety at the Derby Street/Congress Street intersection and a Community Preservation Plan comment request. The group approved prior minutes with edits and supported an e-bikes maintenance workshop.
decisions: Approved the 8/5/2026 and 9/2/2026 minutes with edits, with all members voting in favor.

plain_text:
1 
 
DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
 
 
Salem Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee 
 
Wednesday, September 7, 2026 | 6:15 p.m. 
 
City Hall Annex 1st Floor Meeting Room & Via Remote Participation 
 
Members Present: Josiah Guthrie (Vice Chair, presiding), Kevin Jordan, Alexa Ogno, 
Craig Bilodeau, Matt Caruso 
Members Absent:  Annie Wolf, Josh Nagle 
Also Present:  Tom Devine, Senior Planner 
 
*Technical difficulties prevented Zoom participation until approximately 7:30pm. 
 
Call Meeting to Order 
 
Guthrie calls the meeting to order. Wathne is unable to participate due to technical 
difficulties. 
 
Public Comment 
 
A resident of Jefferson Ave. notes that the abundance of patching on Jefferson Ave. is 
problematic for cyclists. 
 
Discussion of Dept. of Public Services Operations with Ray Jodoin, Director 
(Invited) 
 
Devine introduces DPS Director Ray Jodoin and expresses gratitude for his work and 
commitment to the City. Committee members and Jodoin introduce themselves. 
 
The committee thanked the Director for his work and acknowledged the challenges 
facing the DPW. In discussing current pain points, he explained that the department 
must balance a large workload and public expectations with limited staffing and 
resources. Salem's snow operations cover approximately 104 miles of roadway, 27 
miles of sidewalks and shared-use paths, school routes and bus stops, municipal 
buildings, and fire stations, using 61 snow-removal vehicles and seven additional 
sidewalk machines. 
 
The Jodoin said that responding to major winter storms requires a combination of staff, 
equipment, contractors, and extended work hours. While the city generally has sufficient 
equipment and personnel, it does not always have both available at the same time. He 
acknowledged challenges on North Street during the previous winter and said the DPW 
is working with the Transportation Department on improvements. He also emphasized 
the need for public patience during snow events.
2 
 
 
The committee discussed what residents can realistically expect during storms. Jodoin 
explained that crews must prioritize resources, particularly routes serving schools and 
other critical destinations. Bilodeau suggested adding an automatic response to the 
snow-related email account, which is actively monitored during storm events. 
 
Questions were raised about maintaining bicycle and pedestrian facilities. Jodoin said 
snow-clearing challenges are driven more by facility width, available equipment, and 
staffing than by whether a bike lane is at street or sidewalk level. The group also 
discussed snow removal on North Street, alternative snow-handling methods, and the 
lack of a formal program to help seniors clear snow. 
 
The committee then explored ways it could support the DPW through infrastructure 
design, public education, and advocacy for additional resources. Discussion also 
focused on workforce and contractor shortages. Jodoin said fewer contractors are 
interested in snow operations, a challenge shared by many communities, and noted that 
Salem performs more sidewalk snow removal than many municipalities. Interested 
contractors and seasonal workers can apply through the city's online systems. 
 
The group also reviewed street sweeping operations. Most areas are swept twice 
annually, while downtown, major corridors, and denser neighborhoods receive more 
frequent service. Members noted that debris can accumulate in street-level bike lanes 
and suggested additional attention to those facilities. 
 
A resident of Warren Court, who reported being unable to hear the meeting audio while 
attending remotely, expressed concern that city operations often prioritize automobile 
travel over bicycling and cited examples such as temporary facilities and road closures 
affecting bike travel. She said she would like to help improve conditions for cyclists and 
also raised concerns about the angle of floodlights in her area. Jodoin agreed to discuss 
the lighting issue with the Fire Chief. 
 
Another resident raised concerns about deteriorated pavement and debris on Jefferson 
Avenue following utility work and requested more frequent street sweeping. Jodoin 
noted that the roadway has been impacted by recent utility projects, said he would look 
into the pavement concerns, and explained that Jefferson Avenue is currently swept 
twice per year. 
 
The meeting concluded with discussion of parking and traffic concerns at the Willows 
and a broader conversation about how the committee can continue supporting DPW 
efforts. Guthrie thanked Jodoin for the productive discussion and invited continued 
collaboration, while Jodoin encouraged members to reach out with additional questions. 
 
Discussion of Bike Master Plan and Role of the Committee
3 
 
Ogno has looked into opportunities for larger nonprofits to have a local chapter. 
MassBike doesn’t do chapters, but has affiliated organizations. People for Bikes is more 
of an industry group with expensive memberships fees. 
 
Devine reports that there is now an intern looking into how bike advocacy groups work 
in other communities and he expects the findings to be helpful as the Committee 
reflects on its role. Guthrie wishes to invite the intern for a conversation over coffee. 
 
Devine states that the Mayor is keeping the total committee membership at 9 for now. 
The Council action creating the committee allows for 7 to 11 members. At the same 
time, he notes that the newly appointed member is a transportation planner who has a 
lot to offer the city. 
 
Bikeshare Program Updates 
 
To follow up on Ogno’s question at the previous meeting: Devine reports that e-bikes 
are about 20% of Salem’s Bluebikes fleet but they account for 36% of rides.  Ogno asks 
if there has been any problem with empty and full stations downtown as the tourist 
season ramps up. Devine states that he has heard not complaints, but that doesn’t 
mean Bluebikes customer services isn’t hearing any. Lyft tracks empty and full stations 
and how it compares to the contractual target and this will be reviewed some time after 
October. 
 
Events 
 
The group supports hosting an upcoming MassBike/CEC e-bikes maintenance 
workshop. Last year’s similar event was a success and hosting these events is a small 
way to support MassBike as a partner. 
 
Ogno states that the Taco Trail Ride was rained out on 9/27/2026 and is rescheduled to 
begin at noon at Derby Warf on 10/18/2026. 
 
Bike Safety Updates 
 
Ogno described safety concerns at the Derby Street/Congress Street intersection. 
During a bike bus ride with about a dozen participants, including several young children 
riding independently, the group struggled to make a left turn from Derby Street onto 
Congress Street and became stuck waiting for a walk signal that did not activate. 
Drivers grew impatient and began maneuvering around the group, creating a stressful 
situation. Councilor Turowski was present and observed the difficulties. 
 
The following week, riders used the sidewalk and crossed as pedestrians instead, but 
the experience remained challenging. Ogno noted that, with the school relocation, more 
students must navigate this intersection and expressed concern that transportation 
improvements are focusing on roadway segments without adequately addressing 
difficult intersections, which are often the biggest barriers to safe travel.
4 
 
 
The group wishes to receive details from the police regarding crashes that involve 
bikes. 
 
Ongo described the new “Neighborway” in Somerville and its success in slowing cars to 
safe speeds. The group wishes  to discuss neighborways at the next meeting. 
 
Annual Community Preservation Plan Request for Input 
 
Guthrie feels that the comment request is short notice, which may limit the group’s 
feedback this year but leave the opportunity to be more proactive next year. The group 
discusses the limited references to bikes in the plan. They highlight the need to make 
sure that the bike racks which the plan encourages are the optimal type. Guthrie will 
share a draft comment letter for the group’s review. 
 
Staff Update 
 
Devine states that all his updates have been covered under earlier agenda items. 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
The group identifies misspelling of Devine and Guthrie in the minutes. 
 
Ogno motions, Bilodeau seconds, and all vote in favor to approve the 8/5/2026 and 
9/2/2026 minutes with edits. 
 
Adjourn 
 
Bilodeau motions, Ogno seconds, and all vote in favor to adjourn at 8pm. 
 
*** 
 
*These minutes were generated with the assistance of Microsoft Copiliot AI.
